This SQL is the same scope written out, for when you must extend it.","SCOPE IS ONE HARMONIZED ENTITY, NOT A NAME PREFIX. A bare `UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'SIEMENS%'` over-counts: it also counts sibling entities, for example the SIEMENS HEALTHCARE, SIEMENS MOBILITY, SIEMENS ENERGY and SIEMENS GAMESA RENEWABLE ENERGY groups. Measured 2026-09-30 on patstat_2026_spring for 2016-2026: 68,965 applications for the bare prefix against 32,497 for the endpoint's entity, 2.1 times more. Keep the regexp_replace equality, and replace 'SIEMENS' in it with the entity key: the name in upper case, `.` and `,` removed, and trailing legal forms such as AG, GMBH, CORP or LTD removed.","Resolve first when the name is not a single entity: SELECT ap.name, COUNT(DISTINCT ap.application_id) FROM flowleap.applicants ap WHERE UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'X%' GROUP BY ap.name ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 15 (interpretation_conventions.entity_disambiguation). Several different keys in that list are several entities: ask which one, never add them together.","This SQL returns 32,503 applications, 6 more than the endpoint's 32,497, one each in six year-office cells. The endpoint groups only the 200 largest names that match the prefix, so it misses rare spellings of the same entity (SIEMENS COMPANY, SIEMENS LTD., SIEMENS CORP). Quote the endpoint's number.","`granted` here counts every office. The endpoint reports WO, ES and PL grants as null and leaves them out of its totals, so this column is higher (9,288 against the endpoint's 8,281 for 2016-2026)."],"logical_sql":"SELECT a.office, a.filing_year,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.application_id) AS applications,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.granted THEN a.application_id END) AS granted
FROM flowleap.applications a
JOIN flowleap.applicants ap ON ap.application_id = a.application_id
WHERE UPPER(ap.name) LIKE 'SIEMENS%'

","question":"In which states does {applicant} let its EP patents lapse, and when?"},{"logical_sql":"WITH hits AS (

content.text:
Perovskite tandem filings are classified almost entirely in H10K (organic/hybrid devices) and H10F (inorganic photovoltaics), with Y02E10/549 as a near-universal tag. The discriminating codes are H10K30/57 and H10K39/15 on the H10K side and H10F10/19 and H10F10/161 on the H10F side.

Source: PATSTAT 2026 Spring, English-language titles and abstracts matching "perovskite tandem", first filed 2013 or later, counted as DOCDB families. The title corpus has 65 families and the abstract corpus 165 families. Corpus size is the total number of families carrying that code in the edition, which tells you whether a code is an area or a tag.

| Code | Scheme title (abbreviated) | Share of title hits | Share of abstract hits | Corpus size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Y02E10/549 | Organic PV cells (Y-tag) | 66% | 66% | 33,924 |
| H10K85/50 | Organic / hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites | 52% | 51% | 3,684 |
| H10K30/57 | Organic PV comprising multiple junctions, e.g. tandem | 51% | 50% | 550 |
| H10K30/40 | p-i-n structure with perovskite absorber | 32% | 33% | 2,809 |
| H10K39/15 | Assemblies of both organic and inorganic PV cells | 28% | 22% | 628 |
| H10F10/19 | PV cells with multiple potential barriers of different types (PN + PIN tandem) | 19% | 26% | 354 |
| H10F10/161 | Multiple PN heterojunctions, e.g. tandem cells | 15% | 18% | 661 |
| H10K30/10 | Organic/inorganic heterojunctions | 15% | 23% | 1,988 |
| H10F10/142 | Multiple PN homojunctions, e.g. tandem | 11% | 12% | 634 |
| H10F19/40 | Mechanically stacked PV cells (4-terminal tandems) | 8% | 12% | 445 |
| Y02P70/50 | Manufacturing tag | 15% | 29% | large |

How to read this:

- **The tandem-specific codes** are H10K30/57, H10K39/15, H10F10/19, H10F10/161, H10F10/142 and H10F19/40. Each has a corpus of a few hundred families, so they define the area rather than tagging it.
- **H10K30/57 versus H10F10/19** splits by where the examiner put the emphasis. Perovskite-on-perovskite and general perovskite tandems land in H10K30/57. Perovskite-on-silicon tandems pick up H10F10/19 or H10F10/161 for the silicon bottom cell, often alongside H10K39/15 for the organic-plus-inorganic assembly.
- **H10K85/50 and H10K30/40** identify the perovskite absorber, not tandem architecture. They appear on any perovskite cell, so use them only in an AND with a tandem code.
- **Y02E10/549** sits on two thirds of hits and on 34,000 families in total. It is a tag, not a search anchor.
- **Secondary codes** worth knowing: H10K30/82 and H10F77/244 for transparent recombination or top electrodes, H10K30/88 for encapsulation, H10K71/12 for solution processing, and H01G9/2009 as a legacy dye-sensitised-cell lineage on a small minority.

Two caveats. This edition contains no H01L31 or H01L51 codes on the corpus at all, so the reclassification to H10F and H10K is complete in PATSTAT. Google Patents still carries legacy H01L codes, so a search there should add H01L31/078 and H01L51/42 variants. Second, the text match is English-only, which excludes most Chinese-language filings. A cross-check seed of "perovskite stacked/laminated solar cell" returned 1,470 families but only 7% carried H10K30/57, because "laminated" in translated Chinese abstracts usually means a layered single-junction cell, so I did not rely on it.

A recommended search anchor for landscaping is: H10K30/57 OR H10K39/15 OR H10F10/19 OR H10F10/161 OR H10F19/40, intersected with H10K85/50 OR H10K30/40 to keep the perovskite constraint.
